title: Multiple Linear Regression II: Study Q&A
description: Source-grounded review of categorical variables, joint inference, ANOVA, and combined models.

questions.question: Explain binary variables and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: A factor with c categories is represented with c-1 binary indicators when an intercept is present; the omitted level is the reference.

questions.question: Explain reference levels and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Changing the omitted category changes coefficient interpretations and individual t-ratios, but not fitted values or the overall model fit.

questions.question: Explain general linear hypothesis and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Joint restrictions are expressed as H0: Cβ=d, with C chosen for the scientific question.

questions.question: Explain partial f test and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Compare a reduced nested model with a full model: F=((Error SS)reduced-(Error SS)full)/(p s²full).

questions.question: Explain term life example and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Testing MAR0 and MAR2 jointly gives F=3.235 with p=2 and 269 denominator degrees of freedom; the reported p-value is 0.0409.

questions.question: Explain one-factor anova and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: The model yᵢⱼ=μⱼ+εᵢⱼ estimates each group mean by its sample average and partitions total variation into factor and error sums of squares.

questions.question: Explain auto claims anova and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: For 18 risk classes and 6,773 claims, log-claim ANOVA reports Factor SS 39.2, Error SS 7729.0, and Error MS 1.14.

questions.question: Explain ancova and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: A factor and covariate can have variable intercepts with a common slope, or both intercepts and slopes can vary by group.

questions.question: Explain hospital costs and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: The pooled plot suggests a negative association, but DRG-specific relationships show why an omitted factor can mislead; the variable-slope test is F=13.535.

questions.question: Explain interactions and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Interactions permit effects such as slopes to differ by category; with two factors they can be interpreted as a combined factor.

questions.question: Explain general linear model and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Continuous, transformed, and categorical predictors can enter linearly in coefficients; coefficient estimates can be nonunique under linear dependence.

questions.question: Explain unique fitted values and its role in Chapter 4.
questions.answer: Even when parameter estimates are not unique, least-squares fitted values, residuals, and error sums of squares are unique.

questions.question: How should the exercise involving several coefficients be analyzed?
questions.answer: Express the requested restrictions as Cβ=d, identify full and reduced nested models, and use the partial F construction described in Section 4.2.

questions.question: For the Automobile Insurance Claims exercise, what model structure is relevant?
questions.answer: Use the one-factor ANOVA formulation for risk class and the supplied AutoClaims data; estimate class means and use the factor/error sum-of-squares decomposition as requested.

questions.question: How should an interaction exercise be interpreted?
questions.answer: Specify the main effects and interaction terms, then translate fitted differences or slopes back to the corresponding factor combinations.
